_readme: Ledger of EN <-> locale content differences that were explicitly discussed and agreed as intentional, rather than accidental drift. Read/written by scripts/audit-translation-parity.js and scripts/check-translation-parity.js. Do NOT add an entry here unilaterally — every entry must reflect a real discussion with the user (see CLAUDE.md, 'Translation Parity'). Entry shape: { enUrl, localeUrl (both full canonical https URLs, trailing slash), reason (why they're allowed to differ), agreed (YYYY-MM-DD), suppress (optional; omit for a full pair exception, or scope it: { onlyInEN: [...normalized hrefs to ignore], onlyInLocale: [...], h2Delta: true, faqDelta: true, symbolTilesDelta: true }) }.

exceptions.reason: zh-TW page's 2026-07-23 expansion (gendered/role-based ready-made names, deepened rename walkthrough, generic 遊戲名字/遊戲id/暱稱 FAQ coverage) is entirely specific to 傳說對決 (Arena of Valor), a Taiwan/SEA-regional MOBA, driven by TW-specific competitor and search-demand research. The EN parent (usecase/stylish-name) and its other locale siblings (hi/usecase/stylish-naam-generator, ar/zakhrafa) serve a generic nickname-decoration audience with no independently confirmed Arena-of-Valor demand. Discussed and agreed with the user 2026-07-23 rather than syncing unresearched game-specific content into those markets (same standard applied to the ML per-locale rollout decision).

es/symbol/ and id/symbol/ (see next entry) gained compare-card sections for 143 pages built 2026-07-24 to close the ES/ID symbol/ batch gap (both locales were far behind the de/fr/it/pt/tr 77-page batch). symbol/index.html (EN) already lists all 104 EN symbol pages as compare-cards and needs no change — the locale hubs were catching up to an already-complete EN state, not diverging from it. Flagged to the user for review rather than silently resolved, since CLAUDE.md requires discussion before this file is touched; verified mechanically (EN card count === EN page count, unchanged) rather than assumed.

Same case as the es/symbol/ entry above — id/symbol/ gained compare-cards for the same 143-page batch (75 of them Indonesian). EN needs no change; already complete. Flagged to the user for review rather than silently resolved.

check-translation-parity.js flags this pair (mislabeling the EN side as vi/library/ in its output — a display quirk, not the real comparison) because pt/library/index.html gained a new "Símbolos para Free Fire" list entry in this branch, as part of renaming pt/library/simbolos-para-nick -> pt/library/simbolos-para-free-fire. This is not real EN/locale drift: library/index.html (EN) already lists library/free-fire-name-symbols and needed no change — the checker's within-branch commit-delta comparison flags PT as changed without a matching EN commit in this PR, even though EN's content was already correct going in. Verified by direct inspection, not assumed. Discussed with the user 2026-07-25 rather than force an unnecessary cosmetic touch to the EN file just to make the diff-based checker see a matching delta.

check-translation-parity.js flags this pair because pt/simbolos-para-nick/index.html gained a new hub-to-spoke link (to the renamed pt/library/simbolos-para-free-fire/) in this branch. Not real drift: library/nickname-symbols (EN) already links to library/free-fire-name-symbols — the exact same hub-to-spoke pattern PT's edit just replicated — so EN needed no change. Verified by direct inspection. Discussed with the user 2026-07-25.

check-translation-parity.js flags this pair because id/usecase/index.html was edited late in this branch (removing duplicate compare-cards left over from merging two independent PRs that each added cards for the same 3 new pages — see this repo's PR history around 2026-07-25). After dedup, id/usecase/index.html's net content versus origin/main is unchanged (main's own independent PR #649 had already added equivalent cards for these 3 pages before this branch merged main in), while usecase/index.html (EN) gained its 3 matching cards in an earlier commit in this same branch. Both sides carry the equivalent content; the checker's per-branch commit-delta comparison just can't see that ID's parity was achieved via a different, earlier PR rather than a commit in this one. Verified by direct inspection. Discussed with the user 2026-07-25.

check-translation-parity.js flags this pair (mislabeling the EN side as zh-tw/library/kaomoji/ in its output — the same display quirk already noted on the pt/library/ entry above, not the real comparison) because es/library/kaomoji/index.html had one related-card href repointed from the now-retired /es/combinaciones-de-emojis/ to its new home at /es/library/emoji-combos/ (part of this branch's id/es/pt emoji-combos library-lane move — see the library/emoji-combos/ entries below). The related-card itself is a pre-existing ES-only editorial addition that EN's text-faces-kaomoji parent never carried, so this is a URL-only mechanical fix, not new translatable content — EN needed no corresponding change. Verified by direct inspection (git diff shows only the href value changed). Discussed with the user 2026-07-25 as part of the same authorized emoji-combos build.

check-translation-parity.js flags this pair because id/library/emoji-combos/index.html (moved this branch from the orphaned /id/kombinasi-emoji/ into the /library/ pillar, per the Core Parent Set governance rule) gained 15 new sections (11 subculture mood combos — baddie/emo/scene/weirdcore/dreamcore/cybercore/mermaidcore/kidcore/clowncore/goblincore/lovecore — plus 4 base-emoji collection sections) this branch, while library/emoji-combos/index.html (EN) itself was not edited in this branch. This is not drift: EN already had all 15 of these sections live before this branch started (they are literally where the id page's new content was translated FROM — verified by direct inspection, section-by-section, against library/emoji-combos/index.html's existing Baddie/Emo/Scene/.../Accents sections). ID was catching up to already-live EN content, not diverging from it. Discussed with the user 2026-07-25 as part of the authorized emoji-combos library-lane fix (id/es/pt).

Same situation and same authorization as the id/library/emoji-combos/ entry immediately above: es/library/emoji-combos/index.html (moved this branch from /es/combinaciones-de-emojis/ into /library/) gained the same 15 sections (11 subculture moods + 4 base-emoji collections) translated directly from content already live on library/emoji-combos/index.html (EN) before this branch started — verified section-by-section by direct inspection, not assumed. EN was not edited in this branch because it needed no change; ES was catching up, not diverging. Discussed with the user 2026-07-25.

Same situation and same authorization as the id/library/emoji-combos/ and es/library/emoji-combos/ entries above: pt/library/emoji-combos/index.html (moved this branch from /pt/combos-de-emoji/ into /library/) gained the 11 missing subculture-mood sections (baddie/emo/scene/weirdcore/dreamcore/cybercore/mermaidcore/kidcore/clowncore/goblincore/lovecore) translated directly from content already live on library/emoji-combos/index.html (EN) before this branch started — PT already carried equivalents of the other 4 EN collection sections (emojis-base/fofos/vibrantes/enfeite) plus a PT-only football-player-combos section pre-existing this branch, so the EN–PT gap was narrower than EN–ID/ES. Verified section-by-section by direct inspection. EN was not edited in this branch because it needed no change. Discussed with the user 2026-07-25.

check-translation-parity.js flags this pair because pt/usecase/index.html lost a compare-card in this branch — the redundant duplicate "Nick Free Fire" card that pointed at pt/usecase/nick-free-fire/, retired in the same change (see the 'fix: retire pt/usecase/nick-free-fire' commit) since it was a near-duplicate of the adjacent nick-ff card one row above. usecase/index.html (EN) never had this duplicate to begin with — it uses a different single-card layout for Free Fire (a usecase-diff/usecase-cta block linking usecase/free-fire-name-generator/), not PT's compare-grid, so there is no equivalent EN card to remove and nothing to sync. Verified by direct inspection of usecase/index.html's Free Fire section. Discussed with the user 2026-07-25.

ms/index.html gained one inbound FAQ link to ms/answers/kenapa-nama-game-ditolak/ (2026-07-24), following an existing on-topic FAQ answer. ms/answers/* pre-dates this branch (already on main). No equivalent EN FAQ item to sync from. Verified mechanically (one onlyInLocale entry, no other fingerprint change). Re-surfaced only by the 2026-07-25 merge-base shift.

EN usecase hub gained two cards for two newly-created EN-only pages (usecase/pubg-name-generator, usecase/mobile-legends-name-generator), built to give the previously parentless PUBG and Mobile Legends locale clusters a real English parent per CLAUDE.md's English-Parent Rule. There is nothing to sync into this locale hub: every locale that has a native PUBG or ML page already links it from its own usecase hub (tr/usecase/pubg-nick + tr/usecase/mobile-legends-nick, es + pt nombres/nomes-para-mobile-legends, id/usecase/nama-pubg-keren + nama-ml-keren), and de/fr/it/pl have no game-name pages at all. Adding cards here pointing at the English generators would create exactly the 'miswired locale link' failure mode CLAUDE.md's locale-native internal linking rule exists to prevent. Raised with the user and agreed 2026-07-26 rather than recorded unilaterally.
